{
  "dataset_name": "pima_diabetes",
  "model_family": "linear_svm",
  "schema_generator": "gemini-2.5-pro",
  "schema_version": "1.1",
  "features": [
    {
      "name": "glucose_severity_score",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "A continuous measure of plasma glucose concentration exceeding a high-risk threshold (140 mg/dL), creating a linear risk ramp.",
      "value_range": [
        0.0,
        58.0
      ],
      "feature_family": "Glucose Metabolism",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Provides a smooth, continuous feature that directly correlates with a primary risk factor, which is ideal for a linear model's decision boundary.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.maximum(0, plas - 140.0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "bmi_risk_score",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "A continuous measure of Body Mass Index (BMI) exceeding the overweight threshold (25 kg/m^2).",
      "value_range": [
        0.0,
        24.6
      ],
      "feature_family": "Body Composition",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Captures the severity of being overweight as a continuous variable, which helps the linear model weigh this risk factor appropriately.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.maximum(0, mass - 25.0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "insulin_resistance_proxy",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "A scaled interaction term between insulin and plasma glucose, serving as a proxy for insulin resistance.",
      "value_range": [
        0.0,
        114.7
      ],
      "feature_family": "Glucose Metabolism",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Combines two key variables into a single, powerful predictor that can improve linear separability by capturing a key physiological mechanism.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "(insu * plas) / 1000.0"
    },
    {
      "name": "age_x_bmi_interaction",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "An interaction term between age and BMI, capturing the compounded risk of high BMI at an older age.",
      "value_range": [
        0.0,
        3571.2
      ],
      "feature_family": "Composite Risk",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Allows the linear model to account for the non-linear synergistic effect of two important risk factors, improving the model's complexity without changing its family.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "age * mass"
    },
    {
      "name": "blood_pressure_severity",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "A continuous measure of diastolic blood pressure exceeding a pre-hypertension threshold (80 mm Hg).",
      "value_range": [
        0.0,
        42.0
      ],
      "feature_family": "Cardiovascular",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Isolates and quantifies the risk associated with high blood pressure, providing another clear, linear signal for the model.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.maximum(0, pres - 80.0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "body_fat_proxy",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "An interaction term between BMI and skin thickness, intended as a proxy for total body fat.",
      "value_range": [
        0.0,
        2976.0
      ],
      "feature_family": "Body Composition",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Creates a composite feature that may be a better linear predictor of metabolic health than either BMI or skin thickness alone.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "mass * skin"
    },
    {
      "name": "pregnancy_frequency",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "The number of pregnancies normalized by the approximate number of childbearing years (age minus 20).",
      "value_range": [
        0.0,
        13.0
      ],
      "feature_family": "Reproductive History",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Creates a rate-based feature that may better capture the metabolic load of pregnancies than the raw count, providing a more nuanced signal.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where(age > 20, preg / (age - 20.0), 0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "glucose_per_unit_insulin",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "The ratio of plasma glucose to serum insulin, which can be an indicator of insulin sensitivity. A small amount is added to insulin to prevent division by zero.",
      "value_range": [
        0.0,
        198.0
      ],
      "feature_family": "Glucose Metabolism",
      "expected_model_benefit": "This ratio directly models a physiological relationship relevant to the outcome, potentially creating a feature with strong linear separation power.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "plas / (insu + 1.0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "genetic_predisposition_score",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "The diabetes pedigree function, representing a synthesized score of genetic risk from family history.",
      "value_range": [
        0.096,
        1.461
      ],
      "feature_family": "Genetic",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Directly incorporates a pre-computed risk score, which is expected to have a monotonic relationship with the outcome, making it suitable for a linear model.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "pedi"
    },
    {
      "name": "age_decade",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Age of the individual scaled by a factor of 10.",
      "value_range": [
        2.1,
        7.2
      ],
      "feature_family": "Demographics",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Scales the age feature to be more in line with other engineered features, which can help with model convergence and interpretation of coefficients in a linear model.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "age / 10.0"
    },
    {
      "name": "metabolic_health_profile",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "A holistic score from 0 to 10 assessing overall metabolic health. The score is based on a combined view of glucose levels (`plas`), BMI (`mass`), and blood pressure (`pres`), where higher scores indicate a poorer profile with multiple risk factors.",
      "value_range": [
        0,
        10
      ],
      "feature_family": "Composite Risk",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Synthesizes information from multiple columns into a single, semantically rich score that aligns with clinical intuition, potentially creating a very strong linear predictor.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "physiologic_stress_score",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "A score from 0 to 10 representing an estimate of overall physiologic stress. This score considers extreme values or unusual combinations of all input variables, such as very high insulin with normal glucose, or zero values for blood pressure or skin thickness, which may indicate data quality issues or severe health anomalies.",
      "value_range": [
        0,
        10
      ],
      "feature_family": "Composite Risk",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Captures complex, non-obvious patterns and potential data anomalies that a simple linear combination of features might miss, providing a distilled risk signal.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    }
  ]
}
